Kimberly / Alex — attaching our pass at the MSA with in-line comments and suggested language. Key legal points summarized here: 

1) Subprocessors / DPA notice window
- We generally require 60 days notice for material changes to subprocessors. For commodity cloud providers we can accept 30 days; for any entity that will touch customer plaintext or logging data we will require 60 days and the right to object.

2) Data processing & deletion
- We flagged SierraFuse’s requested 365-day default for logs as OK for 'request logs' but not for 'security/audit' logs. Recommended language: default request logs 365 days, security/audit 730 days, option to configure via SOW with pricing tiers.

3) Liability and indemnity triangulation
- SierraFuse redline reduces Redwood’s indemnity in a way that could expose enterprise customers. Proposed compromise: retain standard liability cap but add a carveout for third-party IP claims tied to SierraFuse-provided connectors only where SierraFuse has provided the connector codebase or ML artifact.

4) SLA credits / rollback procedures
- Suggested we add a short rollback clause for a failed deployment related to connector updates; this preserves our operational safeguards for canary rollbacks and reduces emergency rollback disputes.

I attached:
- SierraFuse_MSA_redlines_v3_docx_comments.docx (tracked changes + comment bubbles)
- DPA_processing_appendix_sierrafuse.pdf (annotated)

Kimberly / Sergio — thanks for the quick turnaround and the annotated redlines. We reviewed Sergio’s comments with our counsel. Our position on the key items: 

- Subprocessor notice: SierraFuse can accept 60 days for providers that access full plaintext request payloads; however, for performance-sensitive providers (edge caching and CDN) we would like the flexibility of 30 days. We propose a hybrid clause and have a short draft attached.

- Data retention: we can accept the 730-day security log retention as a default if Redwood offers a contractual credit for customers who require less retention (to offset storage cost). We’ve outlined a pricing table in the SOW appendix.

- Liability: SierraFuse cannot accept a carveout that would leave them fully on the hook for third-party IP claims; they propose mutual indemnities with a narrow exception for willful misconduct.

We’ve prepared a DocuSign package with the latest tracked MSA (see link below) — it’s missing a few of the redline responses from Redwood. Please confirm you can review and sign off on the final pass by next Tuesday 08/17 so our procurement can get PO issued.
